title: Eviction-tiering and speculative KV snapshotting for OOM resilience
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Continuous batching combined with long KV caches occasionally triggers GPU OOMs during peak workloads. Current eviction policies are reactive and coarse: global LRU or TTL-based eviction leads to costly full-model fallsbacks and increased tail latency. Goal: implement an eviction-tier + speculative snapshot approach that minimizes hard OOMs by proactively moving low-value KV state off GPU, enabling per-batch soft-shedding, and providing deterministic fast fallback paths (quantized model variant or CPU-staged KV replay) without dropping in-flight requests.
background: Observed multiple incidents where sustained long-context chat sessions + large batch windows caused memory pressure spikes. Recent mitigations (smaller batch caps, aggressive global eviction) reduced frequency but increased latency/cost and harmed throughput. Design alternatives considered: (1) finer-grained LRU with async eviction to host RAM, (2) preemptive KV compression on cold entries, (3) per-request budget enforcement with token-shedding, (4) emergency fallback to smaller/quantized model. We propose combining 1 and 2 with a speculative snapshot mechanism to enable safe async eviction and quick reloads.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook updated and team trained on new metrics and thresholds
Synthetic stress test: reduce OOM frequency by >= 90% under 2x peak workload compared to baseline
Tail latency increased <= 10% at p99 under steady-state compared to current production
Fallback path exercised in canary and rollback tested (must return successful responses within SLA)
End-to-end telemetry shows < 5% requests routed to slow CPU rehydrates during normal load
implementation_steps: Design eviction tiers: HOT (GPU-resident, frequently accessed), WARM (compressed GPU/CPU mirror), COLD (CPU-only snapshot)
Implement per-entry metadata: last_accessed_ts, hot_score, compressed_size (kept compact)
Speculative snapshotter: background thread that checkpoints selected WARM/COLD entries to pinned host memory and marks GPU slot reusable
Async restore path: fast mmap-style rehydrate from host snapshot into a preallocated slot with zero-copy where possible
Per-batch memory budget: compute allowed new-KV bytes per batch; if exceeded, trigger token-shedding or reduce batch window

Fallback orchestration: on imminent OOM, try (1) force-evict COLD snapshot, (2) re-route request to quantized model variant with same semantics, (3) if still failing, enqueue retry with backoff and degraded context
Metrics & tracing: instrument evictions, snapshots, restore latency, quantized-fallback rate, and request-level memory accounting
Canary rollout: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on increased error/tail latency thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for snapshotting correctness and metadata lifecycle
Integration tests simulating batched inference with synthetic KV growth patterns
Chaos tests to simulate preemptive evictions and concurrent restore races (verify no cache corruption)
Load test comparing baseline vs new strategy under varying sequence length distributions
Safety test: intentionally induce restore failure and verify fallback model and retry semantics behave as expected
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Snapshotting CPU memory growth could exhaust host RAM — Mitigation: per-process host-memory quota + eviction LRU on snapshots
Risk: Restore latency spikes when many requests concurrently need rehydrate — Mitigation: rate-limit restores and prioritize high-hot-score entries; use progressive partial rehydrates
Risk: Complexity increases code-paths and potential for subtle bugs — Mitigation: staged rollout, heavy unit/integration tests, feature flag gating
Risk: Quantized model variant has quality regressions for some prompts — Mitigation: maintain per-model quality metrics and only route for low-quality-tolerance customers or internal retries
rollout_and_monitoring: Stage 1 (internal infra-only): shadow mode snapshotter for 2 days and collect metrics
Stage 2 (canary): 10% user traffic, monitor OOMs, p99 latency, quantized-fallback rate for 24h
Stage 3 (ramped): 50% for 48h, then full if stable
Dashboard widgets: snapshot pool utilization, restores/sec, avg restore latency, requests with degraded context, OOM events
Alert thresholds: unexpected OOM spike (>1/hour per cluster), restore latency p95 > 200ms, quantized fallback rate > 2%
notes: We should prefer zero-copy host snapshots where the NIC/CRI allows pinned host pages to avoid extra memcpy
Consider integrating with existing autoscaler to momentarily scale up GPU count when snapshot restore backlog grows beyond threshold
Keep a small pool of preinitialized GPU slots reserved for restores to avoid allocation delays
This ticket intentionally separates speculative snapshot storage from long-term persistence (no durability guarantees)
